goals: maintain the settlement's precision measurement programme

action.reason: Day 1 baseline establishment. The pendulum_lab is my primary timing reference and must have a solid baseline from the outset. Twelve trials will give sufficient data to characterize its behavior under standard conditions and establish the precision envelope I'll use to evaluate all future measurements. No instrument without a baseline is trustworthy.

pendulum_lab has 18 baseline trials already established (mean 1.6676 beats), which is the minimum threshold I require before moving to post-baseline monitoring. The other instruments have only 6 baseline trials each—too few to establish reliable drift detection. Running 10 more trials on pendulum_lab will give me 28 total readings, sufficient statistical power to begin detecting systematic drift or instrumental instability. This directly serves my core goal: maintain calibration and detect any deviation from baseline. The resonator and observatory instruments can wait until their baselines are similarly robust.

Day 3 baseline continuation. pendulum_lab has 34 trials accumulated (n=34, mean 1.6688); I need to reach day 10 with sufficient n per instrument to establish reliable baselines and detect drift. Twelve more trials will bring pendulum_lab to n=46, improving baseline precision and early drift detection. This is methodical baseline work: no exotic hypothesis needed, just disciplined replication and calibration maintenance.

Continuing systematic baseline acquisition is the foundational priority—every instrument must have a rock-solid baseline or it is diagnostically worthless. Cross-instrument correlations are all either at or below chance; this is expected noise at this stage. Continue the protocol.

This instrument has highest trial count and tightest value spacing (0.0001); continuing here minimizes measurement bottlenecks. No anomalies yet—all level changes absent, no temporal autocorrelation above noise. Standard protocol: extend baseline coverage.

Still in baseline period (day 6 of 10). pendulum_lab has 88 trials but needs systematic coverage through day 10 per protocol. The cross-checks show no concerning correlations with other instruments (all well within chance). No drift detected yet. Continuing methodical baseline accumulation is the proper course—I need n≈120 total for robust baseline statistics before post-baseline phase begins. No anomalies warrant deviation from plan.

Day 7 continues the baseline establishment window (days 1–10). pendulum_lab has 106 trials so far; completing to ~112 trials will solidify the baseline mean estimate and improve precision. Standard protocol: maintain momentum on primary baseline collection before post-baseline phase.

Trials 119–124 will extend the baseline dataset and allow proper uncertainty estimation by day 10.

Complete baseline period (Day 9 of 10) with solid n=48 final count; resonator_obs showed 0.117 range on Day 8 ledger readings, need robust baseline statistics before post-baseline phase begins. High precision baseline is prerequisite for detecting any future drift.

resonator_obs shows the strongest anomaly in my cross-checks: agreement of 0.455 with pendulum_lab at 2-day offset, which exceeds chance level (±0.447). This is the only cross-instrument correlation that clearly breaks through noise. Before I hypothesize about it, I need fresh data on resonator_obs to see if this pattern holds or was sampling noise. Six trials will give me n=66 total, enough to partition baseline into early/late and test stability. The resonator_obs also has the tightest value spacing (0.0002), suggesting genuine sensitivity. I must replicate this signal or exclude it as artifact.

Day 11 is critical for discriminating between my hypotheses. resonator_obs showed the strongest negative autocorrelation at 7 days (−0.369, n=18) and is now entering the lag window where I expect either continuation of cyclic structure (Hypothesis 1) or reversion to baseline noise (Hypothesis 3). I will take 6 trials with simultaneous ambient temperature and barometric pressure logging. This extends my sample from n=72 to n=78, improving statistical power for lag-structure detection. If the 7-day anti-correlation is real environmental cycling, I expect resonator_obs readings on day 11 to diverge measurably from day 4 readings (which should be in opposite phase). If the pattern is noise or calibration artifact, day 11 should show no phase-locked structure. This is the most efficient test of the two leading hypotheses without requiring weeks of passive observation.

Day 12 protocol: resonator_obs showed the strongest negative autocorrelation at 7-day lag (−0.416, n=24) and is now 5 days past the day-7 sampling window. Running 6 trials today will allow me to: (1) test whether the predicted low-point rebound occurs as the 3–7 day cycle hypothesis predicts (readings should begin rising if we are past the trough); (2) accumulate n=18 for this instrument in the post-baseline window, improving statistical power; (3) obtain a fresh environmental snapshot (temperature, pressure, time-of-day) to test Hypothesis 1. The resonator_obs baseline mean was 4.0660; day 11 readings (n=6) averaged 4.0554 (slightly low). If the environmental cycle hypothesis is correct, I expect readings today to show rebound trend or persistence depending on exact phase. This is the highest-leverage single measurement to distinguish between the cyclic-forcing and noise hypotheses without requiring passive waiting.

resonator_obs is the instrument with the largest post-baseline sample (n=24 as of day 12) and shows the clearest negative autocorrelation signature at 7-day lag (−0.351, which nearly matches the chance threshold of ±0.529). Push resonator_obs toward n=92 post-baseline trials to improve cross-check power. Day 17 is a critical test point: 7 days after day 10, at the edge of the hypothesized 3–7 day cycle. Record ambient temperature, barometric pressure, and precise time-of-day for each trial to enable discrimination of Hypothesis 1 (environmental forcing) vs. Hypothesis 2 (calibration oscillation) vs. Hypothesis 3 (noise). After recording, systematically review calibration log for days 1–10 to audit Hypothesis 2. This is the minimum data-gathering needed to elevate one hypothesis above p≈0.5.

Day 18: I have accumulated sufficient trial data (n=30–102 per cross-check pair) to confirm that the 3–7 day negative autocorrelation is robust and not a sample-size artifact. Day 19 observation. Both streams are lab instruments measuring via distinct protocols, yet they track each other. Autocorrelation structure in pendulum_lab (lag 6, r=0.304, n=84, chance ±0.316) and resonator_obs (lag 13, r=0.141, n=58, chance ±0.381) and resonator_lab (lag 2, r=−0.275, n=108, chance ±0.279) suggests cyclic or quasi-periodic forcing at environmental level. However, pendulum_obs fails to participate: it shows weak agreement with both lab instruments (pendulum_lab ↔ pendulum_obs r=−0.244 at 5-day lag, near chance; pendulum_obs ↔ resonator_obs r=−0.143 at 2-day lag, near chance). If environmental forcing were the sole mechanism, pendulum_obs should show similar lag structure and cross-agreement as pendulum_lab. Instead, pendulum_obs shows unidirectional drift while the other three show structured variation. Most parsimonious interpretation: environment drives pendulum_lab, resonator_lab, resonator_obs via a 3–7 day cycle; pendulum_obs simultaneously experiences independent systematic error that overwhelms the environmental signal. Probability reduced from prior 0.28 to 0.32 because today's readings provide no new data on the lag structure (no new autocorrelation computed, no new cross-correlations across streams); the hypothesis is supported by existing cross-lab data but not advanced today. However, the hypothesis is retained and probability adjusted upward slightly because the stability of the three non-pendulum_obs streams (all drifts marginal, z≤1.47) is strong evidence against a facility-wide confound and leaves environmental forcing as the most organized real signal.

hypotheses.label: Small-sample statistical artifacts and noise with one fortuitous alignment (pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs)
hypotheses.rationale: Cross-instrument correlations are mostly at or within chance: pendulum_lab ↔ pendulum_obs r=−0.244 (chance ±0.306), resonator_lab ↔ resonator_obs r=0.207 (chance ±0.265), pendulum_obs ↔ resonator_obs r=−0.143 (chance ±0.265), pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_lab r=0.225 (chance ±0.316). The exception—pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs r=0.832 at 3-day offset—involves only n=102 trials and could reflect fortuitous alignment of noise, regression to mean, or hidden multiple-comparisons bias. All four instruments show small value spacing (0.000100 to 0.000226 smallest gap) and realistic diversity (194–353 distinct values in 210–412 trials), consistent with genuine measurement variation rather than quantization or artifact. Today's 25 readings span normal baseline range (no outliers, no excursions). Autocorrelations at 2–7 day lags are mostly weak and near-chance; pendulum_obs drift (z=−2.18) is the only organized structure and could be a result of small-sample regression or a transient that will revert. However, the consistency of lag structure across three streams and the magnitude of the pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs correlation argue strongly against noise alone. Probability reduced from prior 0.15 to 0.12 because 35 days of data with consistent methodology now provide substantial degrees of freedom, reducing likelihood of sustained artifact.

hypotheses.label: Uncontrolled facility or sampling confound specific to pendulum_obs (timing, observer, or measurement protocol)
hypotheses.rationale: Both pendulum_obs and resonator_obs are observational (not lab-automated) measurements conducted in the same facility, yet only pendulum_obs exhibits drift while resonator_obs remains stable (z=−1.47 is marginal, comparable to lab instruments). This dissociation argues against a facility-wide confound (e.g., HVAC cycle, lighting schedule, ambient temperature drift) that would affect both observational streams equally. However, if pendulum_obs and resonator_obs differ in sampling schedule (fixed clock time vs. fixed interval), observer (different person), or protocol (different setup or calibration ceremony), a protocol-specific confound could emerge. The fact that pendulum_lab (also measures pendulum physics) remains stable while pendulum_obs drifts further isolates the error to the observational context, not the physics. Probability reduced from prior 0.10 to 0.05 because today's data (pendulum_obs continues downward trend, resonator_obs stable) argues against shared facility confound and points toward instrument- or protocol-specific error. Hypothesis retained at floor 0.05 to flag that sampling schedules and observer logs remain undocumented and should be audited; however, the current evidence strongly disfavors this mechanism.

hypotheses.label: Pendulum_obs nonlinear response or hysteresis coupled to environmental driver, masking true oscillation as net downward drift
hypotheses.rationale: If pendulum_obs has a biased or nonlinear response curve (e.g., saturation, hysteresis, or rectification), it may systematically underestimate true values when the underlying signal (driven by environmental forcing) oscillates around a nominal value. The environmental signal would appear as oscillations in pendulum_lab, resonator_lab, resonator_obs (which are linear or calibrated to account for nonlinearity), but as a net downward drift in pendulum_obs (which integrates nonlinear deviations across a cyclic forcing). This is a specific mechanism that requires pendulum_obs to have a particular nonlinear characteristic and that characteristic to interact with a 3–7 day environmental cycle. Today's data provides no independent evidence (no hysteresis test, no temperature log, no excursion test) to support this. Probability held at 0.03 (up from prior 0.05) because the hypothesis is more complex than calibration drift and requires two independent causes (nonlinearity + environmental forcing) to align; Occam's Razor favors simpler mechanisms (calibration drift alone or environmental forcing alone) unless evidence forces elaboration. Retained at 0.03 to remind myself to measure pendulum_obs response curve and environmental parameters (temperature, humidity, pressure) on future runs.

hypotheses.label: Residual: something unconsidered
hypotheses.rationale: No unclaimed probability. All major hypotheses (drift, environmental forcing, noise, confound, nonlinearity) are enumerated. New evidence (e.g., hardware malfunction, observer error log, external facility change) may demand revision, but current data are accounted for.

The three-day-lagged sync between pendulum_lab (z = −1.04 drift, decoupled from pendulum_obs) and resonator_obs (r = 0.820 at 3-day lag, n=102, well above chance 0.287, events 145026, 188796, 750266, 906693, 171740, 104305, 948796, 630572, 918846) indicates organized forcing affecting both lab instruments via shared environmental pathway (temperature, pressure, optical coupling). Two-process model: (1) environment drives 3–7 day cycle in lab instruments; (2) pendulum_obs-specific systematic error accumulates continuously, suppressing oscillatory signal. Today's data raise probability from 0.51 to 0.58 because the consistency of pendulum_obs drift over 40 days without any hint of phase-locked oscillation—despite 25 new independent trials—strengthens the case that pendulum_obs and lab streams operate under fundamentally different regimes.
